 TSP Week in Review: Nov. 9-13, 2026
 November 16, 2026 My Federal Retirement

 We will notify you when they are released. Click here and sign up for the email alert .
 TSP core fund results, Nov. 9-13, 2026. Source: TSP daily share prices. 
 The Thrift Savings Plan (TSP) stock funds rebounded during the week of November 9–13, 2026, recovering nearly all of the previous week’s losses even as a hot inflation report, surging Treasury yields and a leadership shake-up at Nvidia kept the market choppy. The Fixed Income Index Investment (F) Fund was the only core fund to finish lower, as bond prices fell when yields rose.
 The Common Stock Index Investment (C) Fund gained 2.54%, the Small Cap Stock Index Investment (S) Fund gained 2.13% and the International Stock Index Investment (I) Fund gained 2.57%. Each ended the week within about a quarter of a percentage point of its October 30 price, which means the prior week’s drop has been mostly erased. The F Fund fell 1.49%, while the Government Securities Investment (G) Fund edged up 0.10%.
 The Monday Rebound
 Stocks surged Monday, November 9, as a sharp drop in oil prices eased worries about inflation. Reports described it as the market’s best day since April, with all 11 sectors of the S&P 500 finishing higher. The C Fund rose 2.35%, the S Fund jumped 3.44% and the I Fund gained 2.90%.
 The rally came even though Nvidia, one of the market’s most influential stocks, fell after its board opened an investigation into its chief executive over the weekend. Because the Lifecycle (L) Funds blend the core funds, the longer-dated ones that hold the most stock gained about 2.66% on Monday, while L Income gained 0.79%.
 What Drove the Week
 Monday: Falling oil prices and a broad rebound from the prior week’s artificial intelligence (AI) sell-off lifted every major index, with industrial and consumer discretionary companies leading the way.
 Tuesday: The October Consumer Price Index (CPI) report showed prices up 0.4% for the month, above the 0.3% economists expected, with core prices up 0.3% against a 0.2% forecast. Hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials added to the pressure, and Treasury yields jumped, with the two-year yield posting its biggest one-day increase since April 2025, according to reports. The S&P 500 slipped 0.38%. The F Fund fell 0.68% because bond prices move opposite to yields, and the C Fund dipped 0.37%.
 Wednesday: Stock markets stayed open for Veterans Day, a federal holiday , but the bond market was closed and the TSP did not post share prices. AI stocks rebounded after CoreWeave reported results that eased some concerns about the AI buildout, and the S&P 500 rose 1.3%. After the close, reports said Nvidia’s board was preparing to remove its chief executive.
 Thursday: Nvidia’s chief executive resigned, AI-linked stocks sold off again and the S&P 500 slipped about 0.35%. Because the TSP skipped Wednesday, Thursday’s share prices reflected both days. Across the two days, the C Fund finished about 1% higher and the F Fund about 0.7% lower. The S Fund, which holds companies outside the S&P 500 and so has little exposure to the AI leaders, slipped about 0.5%.
 Friday: Chip and AI companies led another decline. The S&P 500 fell 0.4%, the Nasdaq composite dropped 0.9% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.1%, with more than 60% of S&P 500 stocks rising. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to about 5.15% from 5.10% on Thursday. The C Fund fell 0.39%, the S Fund 0.37%, and the I and F Funds 0.15% each.
 For the week, the S&P 500 rose about 2.5%, its first weekly gain since October and its best since August, ending a four-week losing streak, according to Associated Press reports. The C Fund’s 2.54% gain tracked the index closely.

 Several Federal Reserve officials signaled support for further rate increases during the week, and traders increasingly priced in a hike at the Fed’s December meeting. That outlook helped push bond yields higher, which is why the F Fund lost ground even as stock funds recovered.

 Where the Year Stands
 The rebound pushed all three stock funds back into double digits for 2026. The year-to-date gains below are measured from the last close of 2025 through November 13.
 I Fund: +13.08%
 C Fund: +11.53%
 S Fund: +10.89%
 G Fund: +4.08%
 F Fund: -1.44%
 For monthly and longer-term results, see the latest TSP fund performance returns . Last week’s losses are covered in the TSP Week in Review for November 2–6 .
 Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly earnings next week, the first test of the stock since the leadership change. Inflation, Treasury yields and the Federal Reserve’s December decision remain the swing factors for the TSP’s stock and bond funds.
 What the Rebound Illustrates
 Two consecutive weeks of large swings show how quickly short-term results can change. The C Fund fell 2.67% the week of November 2–6 and gained 2.54% the week after, leaving it close to where it stood at the end of October.
 The F Fund’s decline is a reminder that bond funds carry interest rate risk: when yields rise, the prices of existing bonds fall. The G Fund, which holds special Treasury securities and does not move with market prices, kept to its steady daily accrual. How much stock, bond and G Fund exposure makes sense depends on time horizon, other sources of income and comfort with short-term swings. The L Funds adjust their mix automatically as each target date approaches.
